_provenance.source: OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance 1.0, Final (2025-09-16) — https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1_0.html
_provenance.section: Appendix D, Key Attestation in JWT format example; and the `jwt` Proof Type section's second example (a proof carrying key attestation data)
_provenance.software_version: n/a — published specification text, not an implementation
_provenance.note: Both spec examples are printed DECODED — a JOSE header and a body, never a compact token — and the proof example writes its attestation as the placeholder `<key attestation in JWT format>`. So unlike `proof-f.1-jwt.json` there is nothing signed to transcribe: what is third-party here is the SHAPE (member names, types, the `kid: "0"` that indexes `attested_keys`), and the test re-encodes these objects into compact JWS form itself. Signatures over them are therefore meaningless by construction, which is the property the App. D reader is supposed to have: it parses without verifying. The attestation's `x5c` is the spec's own truncated placeholder.

claims.iss: <identifier of the issuer of this key attestation>
